OPTIONAL OPENAI PROVIDER GUIDE (v18)

JARVIS v19 defaults to local Ollama and does not require an API key.
Read LOCAL AI GUIDE.txt first. The instructions below apply only if you choose
OpenAI in Tray > AI conversation > AI provider settings.

SETUP
Create your own key at https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
Right-click the JARVIS tray icon > AI conversation > OpenAI settings.
Paste the key into the password field and Save. Select Test AI connection.
The default model is gpt-5.4-mini; change it if your API project needs another.
API requests and web search may incur charges. Your API account needs available
credits or active billing. ChatGPT subscription usage does not fund API-key calls.
Do not paste keys into chat or release files.

The saved key is encrypted for your Windows account at:
%LOCALAPPDATA%\HudWall\openai-key.dat
It is outside the installation folder and excluded from release ZIPs.
Each user configures their own key. This package contains no API key.

TALK NATURALLY
Say Jarvis, followed by your question. Follow-up listening stays active for
90 seconds after a reply, without repeating Jarvis. Say stop conversation
to return to wake-name listening, or stop listening to turn voice off.
The voice menu still controls the microphone, spoken replies and Windows voice.
Existing local app/time/date/wallpaper commands work without an API key.

Open conversation in the AI tray menu provides typed chat, full replies,
tool activity, clickable sources, Stop response, and New conversation.
Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a newline.
Conversation history is held in memory only, with six recent exchanges and
a size limit. New conversation clears context. Restart also clears it.

DATA AND COST
Speech recognition and synthesis use Windows locally. AI questions, recent
conversation context, relevant tool results and requested text excerpts are
sent to OpenAI. This app does not save microphone recordings or chat to disk.
Requests use store:false; OpenAI's applicable data policies still apply.
AI settings allow disabling AI, AI PC tools, or online web search separately.

PC ACCESS
Examples:
Jarvis, find the invoice PDF in my downloads.
Jarvis, open Steam.
Jarvis, find my project notes and summarize the text file.
Jarvis, search the web for the latest space news.

Search finds filenames and folders on accessible fixed drives, prioritizing
common user locations. Each search stops after 10 seconds, 250000 entries
or 40 matches and reports when results are partial. Refine the filename to
continue. Windows file permissions apply; the app does not run as administrator.
Protected locations, directory links and obvious credential files are excluded.
Installed apps are discovered through configured aliases, Start menu shortcuts
and Windows App Paths. Requested files, folders, apps and websites can open.
Text/code file reading returns at most the first 16000 characters.
PDF and Office files can be found/opened; their contents are not extracted.
Scripts, installers, arbitrary shell commands, destructive actions and admin
operations are not AI tools in this release.
Web answers include clickable source URLs in the conversation window.

VERIFICATION
Encrypted key roundtrips, natural speech grammars, real local search/read,
simulated multi-step OpenAI tool exchanges, context/reset, cancellation and
error handling were tested. A live API key is still required to verify your
account's model access, billing and actual OpenAI replies.

Official API setup: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/quickstart
See CHANGELOG.md for the complete release history.
